newsitem.title: USA: US PLAINS CATTLE BIDS FALL, TRADE STALLS -FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: US PLAINS CATTLE BIDS FALL, TRADE STALLS -FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales Wednesday slowed to a standstill following light to moderate sales near midday at $65.00 per cwt, which were steady with Tuesday's top prices, feedlot sources said.

"After the early sales at $65.00, the packer pulled back his bid at $64.00 and was holding firm," a Kansas source said. "The showlist is nowhere near cleaned up, but no one wants to sell below $65.00 either," he said.
About 5,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle, which brought the week-to-date figure near 65,000, sources said.
Sales in Kansas Wednesday totaled about 20,000, bringing the week-to-date total to about 60,000, sources there said.
Several sources said if bids returned to $65.00 packers would be "buried" with cattle.

Sales at $65.00 were off $1.00 from last week's top, but still at a breakeven or slightly profitable level for some cattle owners, sources said. Trade at $64.00, however, put most owners into unprofitable territory, they added.
Fed cattle prices were weakened by a sharp drop in beef values this week following advances last week that curtailed retail demand, sources noted.
